question: What primary group generates the largest portion of daily clinical refuse in health facilities?
explanation: Nurses perform continuous clinical tasks like dressing changes and injections that naturally generate high volumes of medical refuse. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: Poor management of medical refuse primarily increases the risk of what outcome?
explanation: Mismanaged clinical waste exposes both healthcare workers and the external community to pathogens and needle injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h1)

question: Expired drugs and heavy metal solutions belong to which waste category?
explanation: Expired medications and chemical disinfectants require specialized handling categorized under pharmaceutical and chemical waste streams. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why must human tissues and recognizable body parts be separated from general domestic refuse?

options.A: They create foul odors that disrupt routine hospital administration
options.B: They can be recycled into commercial fertilizer products easily
options.C: They represent pathological waste requiring dignified, specialized disposal
options.D: They possess high monetary value for biomedical research laboratories

explanation: Pathological waste contains organic human material that requires incineration or deep burial to maintain public health standards and dignity. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which Nigerian body establishes primary environmental standards for facility operations?

options.B: National Union of Road Transport Workers

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment oversees ecological regulations and enforces standards for waste management across the country. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is the consequence for a healthcare facility that fails to follow regional waste disposal laws?

options.B: Revocation of operating licenses and penalties

explanation: Regulatory bodies penalize non-compliant institutions through heavy fines and potential closure to protect public safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: What color of container is universally utilized for collecting used clinical sharps?
explanation: Sharps must always go into rigid, puncture-proof safety containers to prevent accidental needlestick injuries among staff. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: At what capacity should a clinical waste bag be sealed and removed?
explanation: Removing bags at three-quarters capacity prevents tearing, spills, and accidental exposure during handling and transport. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: What treatment method uses high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious items?
explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to destroy microorganisms on infectious medical items before final disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: Why is open dumping of untreated hazardous medical refuse prohibited?

options.A: It contaminates groundwater and threatens public health
options.B: It lowers the aesthetic beauty of local neighborhoods
options.C: It consumes too much valuable urban real estate
options.D: It creates excessive noise pollution for nearby schools

explanation: Untreated hazardous refuse left in open spaces leaks toxic pathogens and chemicals into soil and water sources. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: What immediate action must a nurse take following an accidental sharps injury?

options.A: Apply common cooking oil to the site
options.C: Wait until the end of the work shift
options.D: Ignore the scratch if bleeding stops

explanation: Immediate reporting and prophylaxis help prevent transmission of bloodborne infections like Hepatitis B and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which practice forms the foundation of standard infection control precautions during waste handling?

options.A: Treating all patient body fluids as potentially infectious
options.B: Disinfecting waste trolleys once every calendar month
options.C: Wearing gloves only when dealing with diagnosed patients
options.D: Washing hands exclusively after finishing the entire shift

explanation: Standard precautions assume every fluid sample carries potential pathogens, ensuring consistent barrier protection for all staff. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: What primary leadership function does a nurse perform regarding waste management on the ward?

options.C: Personally incinerating all hospital refuse off-site
options.D: Monitoring staff to ensure correct waste segregation

explanation: Nurses supervise clinical areas to ensure proper sorting and containment procedures are followed consistently. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)

question: How does professional nursing leadership influence daily clinical safety habits?

options.A: Through annual written examinations on waste theory
options.B: By issuing strict fines for every minor policy infraction
options.C: By delegating all safety responsibilities to patients
options.D: Through continuous mentorship and consistent role modeling

explanation: Effective nursing leadership guides junior personnel by demonstrating correct safety practices and providing ongoing support. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h7)
